\section*{Quantities, letters, and units}
\begin{center}
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{>{\bfseries}l c l c Y}
\toprule
\rowcolor{TEJMist}
Quantity & Letter & Unit & Symbol & Meaning\\
\midrule
Current & $I$ & ampere & A & Rate of electric charge flow.\\
Voltage & $V$ & volt & V & Electrical push between two points.\\
Resistance & $R$ & ohm & $\Omega$ & Opposition to current.\\
Power & $P$ & watt & W & Rate of energy transfer.\\
Energy & $E$ & joule & J & Work supplied or used.\\
Charge & $Q$ & coulomb & C & Amount of electric charge.\\
Time & $t$ & second & s & Duration of an event.\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{center}

\begin{minipage}[t]{0.49\textwidth}
\section*{Significant figures}
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{>{\bfseries\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.31\linewidth} Y}
\toprule
\rowcolor{TEJMist}Situation & Rule\\
\midrule
Multiply or divide & Use the fewest significant figures.\\
Add or subtract & Use the fewest decimal places.\\
During the work & Keep the full calculator value.\\
Final answer & Round once. Include prefix and unit.\\
Engineering form & Use a power of ten in steps of three so a non-zero value is from 1 to less than 1000.\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{minipage}\hfill
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.48\textwidth}
\section*{Common metric prefixes}
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{l c c Y}
\toprule
\rowcolor{TEJMist}Prefix & Symbol & Power & Example\\
\midrule
giga & G & $10^9$ & $2.4\ \mathrm{GHz}$\\
mega & M & $10^6$ & $3.3\ \mathrm{M}\Omega$\\
kilo & k & $10^3$ & $4.7\ \mathrm{k}\Omega$\\
none & none & $10^0$ & $12\ \mathrm{V}$\\
milli & m & $10^{-3}$ & $47\ \mathrm{mA}$\\
micro & $\mu$ & $10^{-6}$ & $220\ \mu\mathrm{F}$\\
nano & n & $10^{-9}$ & $100\ \mathrm{nF}$\\
pico & p & $10^{-12}$ & $22\ \mathrm{pF}$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{minipage}

\section*{Engineering notation examples}
\begin{center}
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{l l l Y}
\toprule
\rowcolor{TEJMist}Original & Engineering notation & Prefix form & Calculator entry\\
\midrule
$0.000\,047\ \mathrm{A}$ & $47\times10^{-6}\ \mathrm{A}$ & $47\ \mu\mathrm{A}$ & \texttt{47 EXP -6}\\
$4700\ \Omega$ & $4.7\times10^3\ \Omega$ & $4.7\ \mathrm{k}\Omega$ & \texttt{4.7 EXP 3}\\
$2\,200\,000\ \mathrm{Hz}$ & $2.2\times10^6\ \mathrm{Hz}$ & $2.2\ \mathrm{MHz}$ & \texttt{2.2 EXP 6}\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{center}
\textbf{Capital letters matter:} $M$ means mega, but $m$ means milli. The calculator may display \texttt{E} instead of $\times10^n$.

\section*{GUESS method}
\begin{center}
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{>{\bfseries\large}c l Y}
\toprule
\rowcolor{TEJMist}Letter & Step & What to write\\
\midrule
G & Given & Known symbols, values, and units.\\
U & Unknown & What must be found and its unit.\\
E & Equation & General equation first, then rearrange it.\\
S & Substitute & Numbers and units in the rearranged equation.\\
S & Solve & Full value, rounded value, prefix, unit, and answer sentence.\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{center}

\begin{minipage}[t]{0.47\textwidth}
\section*{Ohm's law}
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{l c Y}
\toprule
\rowcolor{TEJMist}Find & Formula & Unit\\
\midrule
Voltage & $V=I\times R$ & V\\
Current & $\displaystyle I=\frac{V}{R}$ & A\\[10pt]
Resistance & $\displaystyle R=\frac{V}{I}$ & $\Omega$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{minipage}\hfill
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.50\textwidth}
\section*{Power and energy}
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{l c Y}
\toprule
\rowcolor{TEJMist}Question gives & Formula & Unit\\
\midrule
$V$ and $I$ & $P=V\times I$ & W\\
$I$ and $R$ & $P=I^2\times R$ & W\\
$V$ and $R$ & $\displaystyle P=\frac{V^2}{R}$ & W\\[10pt]
$P$ and seconds & $E=P\times t$ & J\\
$P$ and hours & $E=P\times t$ & Wh\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{minipage}

\begin{tejnote}[Unit checks]
$\mathrm{V}/\mathrm{A}=\Omega$, $\mathrm{V}/\Omega=\mathrm{A}$, $\mathrm{A}\times\Omega=\mathrm{V}$, and $\mathrm{V}\times\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{W}$. Also, $1\ \mathrm{W}=1\ \mathrm{J/s}$ and $1\ \mathrm{Wh}=3600\ \mathrm{J}$.
\end{tejnote}

\begin{minipage}[t]{0.49\textwidth}
\section*{Parallel circuits: more than one path}
\begin{center}
\includegraphics[width=0.94\linewidth]{../schematics/bw/Parallel_Rule_Reference.pdf}
\end{center}
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{l c}
\toprule
\rowcolor{TEJMist}Quantity & General rule\\
\midrule
Voltage & $V_T=V_1=V_2=\cdots$\\
Current & $I_T=I_1+I_2+\cdots$\\
Resistance & $\displaystyle\frac{1}{R_T}=\frac{1}{R_1}+\frac{1}{R_2}+\cdots$\\[10pt]
Two resistors & $\displaystyle R_T=\frac{R_1R_2}{R_1+R_2}$\\[10pt]
Power & $P_T=P_1+P_2+\cdots$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

\textbf{Check:} $R_T<$ every branch resistance.
\end{minipage}\hfill
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.49\textwidth}
\section*{Series circuits: one path}
\begin{center}
\includegraphics[width=0.98\linewidth]{../schematics/bw/Series_Rule_Reference.pdf}
\end{center}
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{l c}
\toprule
\rowcolor{TEJMist}Quantity & General rule\\
\midrule
Current & $I_T=I_1=I_2=\cdots$\\
Voltage & $V_T=V_1+V_2+\cdots$\\
Resistance & $R_T=R_1+R_2+\cdots$\\
Summation & $\displaystyle R_T=\sum_{i=1}^{n}R_i$\\[10pt]
Power & $P_T=P_1+P_2+\cdots$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

\textbf{Check:} the voltage drops add to the source voltage.
\end{minipage}

\begin{tejnote}[Standard 5\% resistor values]
E24 values in each decade: \textbf{10, 11, 12, 13, 15, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 27, 30, 33, 36, 39, 43, 47, 51, 56, 62, 68, 75, 82, 91}. Multiply by a power of ten, for example $47\ \Omega$, $470\ \Omega$, $4.7\ \mathrm{k}\Omega$, or $47\ \mathrm{k}\Omega$.
\end{tejnote}
